# Failure modes

<!-- Generated by `uv run python -m evals.failures --out docs/FAILURE_MODES.md`. Do not edit by hand; tests/test_failures.py fails if this file drifts. -->

Each pipeline row injects one synthetic fault into the real pipeline with offline doubles (a scripted model, a scripted evidence provider,
and a mock HTTP transport for the reference tools), then checks the route, the handoff reason, the trace, and that no unreviewed
answer text reached the browser. These are behavior checks, not clinical validation, and they use no patient text.
Regenerate with `uv run python -m evals.failures --out docs/FAILURE_MODES.md`. Timings are printed by the command and left out of this file so it stays byte-stable.

Result: 18 of 18 cases pass.

## Tool failure modes

These rows run the patient tools directly, with no model: the form tools through `run_form_tool` with a mock RxNorm transport,
the calculators through the registry, and the HTTP surface through the FastAPI test client. Each checks the fixed wording, the
result shape, and that a failed lookup or a missing input never turns into a value.

Result: 6 of 6 cases pass.

| Case | Fault | Expected behavior | Observed | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schedule_duplicate_brand_generic` | RxNorm maps "Tylenol" and "acetaminophen" to the same ingredient RxCUI. | `duplicates` holds one entry naming both medicines, the not-an-interaction-check line is present, and the unrelated medicine is not flagged. | status `available`; duplicates [('acetaminophen', ['Tylenol', 'acetaminophen'])]; 6 RxNorm requests | pass |
| `schedule_rxnorm_unavailable` | The RxNorm service answers HTTP 503 to every request. | Status `unavailable`; every grid row is still returned; duplicates come from exact typed names only, so a brand and its generic are not linked. | status `unavailable`; 4 rows kept; duplicates [('Tylenol', ['Tylenol', 'tylenol'])] | pass |
| `schedule_batch_timeout` | One RxNorm lookup sleeps past the batch budget. | Status `partial` with no exception; the finished lookup is kept, the slow one is `unavailable`, and the batch ends inside the 8 s production budget (patched down here to keep the suite fast). | status `partial`; lookups {'Tylenol': 'matched', 'Slowmed': 'unavailable'}; batch budget patched down from 8 s for speed | pass |
| `steadi_boundary` | STEADI answers sit on either side of the score-4 line, and one item is missing. | Three 1-point items score 3 and are not at risk; fall plus cane scores 4 and is at risk; one missing item returns `missing_inputs` and no score. | 3 points: at_risk False; fall + cane: 4 at_risk True; one item missing: missing_inputs ['rushes_to_toilet'] | pass |
| `bp_alert_first` | One home reading of 185/95 sits among normal readings. | `alerts[0]` is the fixed AHA line and precedes the averages in the result; it also survives an error result. | alerts 1 listed before averages; 15 seated readings; summary `7-day average 122/77 from 15 readings` | pass |
| `tools_endpoint_unknown_key` | `POST /api/tools/label_sections` and the other reference-only keys. | HTTP 404 `Unknown tool.` with no calculator, form tool, or reference lookup executed; reference keys are absent from `GET /api/tools`. | statuses [404] for 5 unknown or reference-only keys; 0 executions; control `bmi` ran once | pass |
